# `tdd stub <TEST-ID>`

Writes throwing stubs so `tdd red` is a real, non-weak Red. Stubs only fill in missing files/functions (real code is never touched). Arity comes from the call site and the return type from the compared literal (`== 3`, `, "s")`, `.is_err()`), falling back to `int`/`i64`/`any`; if the stub does not compile, write it by hand. An unknown REQ on the test is refused when specs exist.

- **ts/js/py**: throwing stubs for the test's missing relative imports. JS/TS also reads multi-line and `import type`/inline `type` imports (types become `export type X = any`), `import * as ns` (`ns.fn(` → exported functions), static calls `Foo.create(` (→ `static create`), and names the test never calls (`CONFIG.max`, `initialState`) become a throwing `Proxy` value instead of a function. Bare package imports that resolve to a workspace package (package.json `name`/`main`/`exports`) or tsconfig path are stubbed in that entry file; unresolvable ones are listed under `! not stubbed:`. Methods are added to an **existing** class only when the receiver is provably that class (`new X().m(`, `v = new X(); v.m(`, a helper that returns only `new X(..)`, `X.m(`); otherwise nothing is added to real code.
- **JS/TS scope (#153)**: namespace members, methods and dynamic imports come only from the shared preamble and selected test, never sibling tests. `v = new Factory().create()` does not make `v` a Factory instance. Missing manifest-declared workspace entries (including conditional/subpath exports) are created at that entry path. In `assert.throws/rejects`, only the expected-error constructor argument implies Error inheritance; the subject under test remains an ordinary class.
- **Python**: skips stdlib and installed packages (including user-site/PYTHONPATH ones); names used in `pytest.raises`/`assertRaises`/`except` become `class X(Exception)`; a module that still holds only stubs gets newly imported names appended.
- **Python submodules (#158)**: `from pkg import api as local` creates `pkg/api.py` from calls to `local` in the selected test only, never sibling calls; the package initializer is left unchanged.
- **Go** (`go test` finds `undefined: X`): `NewX` constructors (`*X`), types, struct-literal fields, methods and fields (up to 4 probe passes); bare `New()` creates type `Pkg`; field access on a returned value creates `<Func>Result` structs. Constructors (`New`, `NewX`) return a zero value (`return &X{}[, nil]`) so only behaviour methods panic and the Red is not setup-origin. `Err*` sentinels become `var ErrX = errors.New("ErrX")` (also for an external `package x_test`, where the stub goes into the imported package and the in-package pass is skipped). The result is compile-checked with `go test -run ^$`; a failing check prints a warning instead of claiming success.
- **Go preservation (#161)**: external-package stubs always allocate a fresh noncolliding filename, preserving existing real and previously generated `_stub.go` files. Existing production `package` declarations determine the generated package name, not directory names or import aliases; compiler-qualified method types use that same package.
- **Rust** (`tests/*.rs` → `src/lib.rs`): free functions and, for capitalised imports, types (`enum` for `Name::Variant`, else a unit struct); `use crate::a::b::{…}` creates missing `src/a.rs`, `src/a/b.rs` and the `pub mod` lines; `use member_crate::a::X` goes into that workspace crate; `== Some(...)`/tuple literals give `Option<…>` returns. Struct fields are inferred only from struct literals; other field access needs a hand-written stub (the Red is rejected as a compile error until then). Red reasons show the panic message.
- **Java** (`Cls.method(` → `src/Cls.java` / `src/main/java`): `new X(a, b)` ctors (typed from literals) and `X.CONST` enums. Instance methods called on `new X(..)` objects (`a.balance()`) are stubbed too.
- **C/C++** (missing `#include "x.h"` → header-only stub; names from compiler diagnostics): headers go into `include/`/`src/` (never shadowing from `tests/`); unknown `foo_t` types get an opaque `typedef struct foo foo_t;`; typed pointer params come from declarations. Stubs are header-only, so drop the missing `.c`/`.cpp` from your build command.
- **C#** (#136, needs the `dotnet` SDK and a test csproj above the test file): `dotnet build` diagnostics are the source of truth — `CS0246`/`CS0103` (missing type), `CS0234` (missing namespace of a `using`), `CS0117`/`CS1061` (missing static/instance member), `CS0019` (operator). Only diagnostics inside the requested test (shared preamble + that test's lines) drive the stubs, in up to 8 build rounds. Types go into the referenced non-test project that matches the `using` namespace (else the only/best-named referenced project, else the test project with a `!` note), one `<Type>.cs` each, marked `// sdd-stub`: exception types (`: System.Exception`), enums (`X.Member`), records (`new X(a: 1)` named args), interfaces (`IFoo`), static classes (`X.Of(..)`) and classes (`new X(..)`, constructor takes `params dynamic[]` so setup never throws); members are `dynamic` (properties with `set` when assigned, `Async` methods return `Task<dynamic>`, factory names `Of/Create/From*/Parse/Zero/…` return their own type) and throw `NotImplementedException`. Real (unmarked) types are never edited: a missing member is reported as `! not stubbed`. The result is `compile-checked` only when the whole build passes. If only OTHER tests of the same project still fail to compile it says `NOT compile-checked` and names the first error (stub those tests next; one project = one compilation); if `dotnet build` cannot run (restore/network) nothing is claimed and nothing is generated. Build errors in referenced production projects (not the test) must be fixed by hand first.
- **PHP / Julia / R**: writes the file the test loads (`require_once`/`include`/`source`) with throwing functions (`LogicException` / `error()` / `stop()`) for unknown calls; PHP also generates classes from `Class::method(`/`new Class` and skips reserved words and `assert*` helpers.
- **JS/TS/Python classes** also get throwing methods for `new C().m(` / `v = C(); v.m(` calls; Java and Rust also get instance methods (Rust: `impl Type` with `new`-style constructors returning `Self`). PHP/C stubs skip classes, functions and types already declared in project files (and PHP built-ins); PHP exception classes extend `\Exception`. Go skips `any` receivers.
- **#107-#118 additions**: existing JS/TS modules get missing exports/consts/class methods appended (existing lines untouched); Python `from pkg import mod` creates `pkg/mod.py`; Go external `_test` packages are stubbed in the imported package dir; Rust stubs use `unimplemented!("T::m")`, `&mut self` and Result/Option returns; Java skips JDK classes, supports `250L`, Maven `gate --changed` uses `-am -amd`; C stubs `(void)` unused params; PHP `use Ns\Cls;` creates PSR-4 files (composer.json `autoload.psr-4`, else `src/`) and `--missing-module` accepts `Class "X" not found`.
- **#130/#131 (honest verdict, scoped, typed)**: stubs cover only the requested test (shared preamble + that test's body). The result line says `compile-checked` only when the compiler confirmed it (Rust: `cargo test --no-run`; C: `cc -fsyntax-only`); otherwise it says `compile NOT verified` (Java, PHP, Julia, ...) or prints the first compile error and `could not fully stub` — never "Red-safe". If `tdd red` still reports a load/compile error, finish the stub by hand (stub is not re-run in a loop). Languages without a generator (e.g. C#) print `nothing to stub`.
  - **Rust**: inline paths (`krate::geo::Point { x: 1 }`) create the module + a struct whose fields are typed from the literal values.
  - **Java**: `T v = X.m(..)` / `assertEquals(Enum.K, x.m())` give the return type; static factories (`of/create/from/zero/..`) return their own class; every call arity becomes an overload; `X.class`/`catch (X`/`assertThrows` exception classes extend `RuntimeException`; `a.f(..).g()` chains get an `<F>Result` class; classes imported from the project's own package are stubbed into that package; methods missing on an existing class are reported as `! not stubbed`, not silently ignored.
  - **C**: argument types come from casts, `&x`, arrays and declarations; `T *v` + `v->f` makes `T` a complete struct (`long f`); pointer results use the declared `T *` for `_t` opaque types.
  - **PHP**: `use PHPUnit\...`/vendor-autoloadable classes are never stubbed; classes used only in `catch`/`throw new` extend `\Exception`; instance methods called on `new C(..)` receivers (`$h->m()`) are stubbed.
  - **Julia**: `using .Mod` wraps the stub file in `module Mod` with `export`; `@test_throws X` creates `struct X <: Exception end`; test-local functions/destructured names and names defined by existing included files are not stubbed.
  - **Python**: for `eng, log = make()` only the tuple slot holding the class instance (`return Eng(..), log`) gets methods; new modules honor pytest `pythonpath` (`pytest.ini`/`pyproject.toml`/`setup.cfg`/`tox.ini`) even if that directory is new.
  - **#147 Python**: all names (classes, exceptions, constants, methods) come from the requested test's scope only (never other tests of the file); a variable rebound to another class (`s = Counter()` … `s = Sub()`) belongs to its latest class; a helper that returns an instance of class X gives methods only to X (other classes built inside the helper get none).
  - **#148 Go**: scoped to the requested test (compile errors for names it does not use are ignored); methods called through a field selector (`r.c.Add(2, 3)`) keep their arguments; bare `New()` returns the type the test names (`*pkg.Store` in a signature/helper parameter) instead of a package-derived one; external-package struct literals keep every field; a stub file holding only methods is reported, never "nothing to stub".
  - **#149 Rust/Java/C++**: Rust `Type::new(..).unwrap()` returns `Result<Self, String>`, calls compared with `None`/`Some(x)` return `Option<_>`. Java: commas inside string/char literals are not argument separators; `assertEquals("lit", C.m(..))` returns `String`; chained static factories (`A.standard().analyze(..)`) get a `<F>Result` class (a list when `.get/.stream/.size` is chained); generic element types (`List<Token>`) are stubbed; generated stubs start with `// sdd-stub:` and later `tdd stub` runs extend them. C++: `ns::Cls v(..); v.m(..)` yields `namespace ns { class Cls {..}; }` with variadic throwing methods (variables are never functions); a C/C++ stub that still does not compile exits 1.
  - **#150 PHP / C#**: PHP project-class detection is namespace-aware (`use App\Query\Parser;` is stubbed at `src/Query/Parser.php` even if `App\Sdl\Parser` exists; `tdd red --missing-module` compares the FQCN); `Cls::CONST` creates a class with `public const`, `Enum::CASE->value` a string-backed `enum` with those cases (plus static methods called on it). C# stubs go into the namespace of the project the test `using`s / is named after (the test's own `.Tests` namespace is stripped), never the test namespace; a type seen as a helper return/parameter/`is X`/`typeof(X)` is a `class`, not a `static class`; `CS1501` (LINQ-name collisions such as `Append`/`Count` on an `IEnumerable` stub) adds the member; our own exception stubs accept members (`ex.Line`); "not stubbed" notes are de-duplicated. **C# limits**: generic types/methods (`Parser<T>`) are not stubbed (one such field in a shared preamble blocks every test of the class — hand-write the skeleton); members are `dynamic`, so lambdas on a stubbed result (`.Select(x => ..)`, CS1977) and `with` expressions (CS8858) do not compile — hand-write typed stubs there.
  - **#151 Julia / TS / JS**: Julia names ending in `!` are stubbed; a missing function of an already-existing *stub-only* included file is appended inside its `module` (and `export`ed) — real code is never edited and is reported instead; the `module` name follows the `using .X` named like the missing include (not the first `using`). TS/JS: names already reachable through a barrel's `export * from` / `export { x } from` are not stubbed over; `new C<T>(..)` counts like `new C(..)`; methods are only stubbed for receivers that really hold the class (`const { b, out } = mk()` with `return { b: new Box(), out }` stubs `b` only, not `out.push`); names ending in `Error`/`Exception` (or used in `toThrow(X)`) become `class X extends Error`; `import * as ns from '../src/ns.js'` no longer invents an `export const js`.
- **Known limits**: C `enum`/full `typedef`s are not stubbed (only opaque/field-accessed `_t` structs); Go `[]byte(x)` params stay `any`; Rust enum payload variants are stubbed as unit; Python attributes on helper-built objects are not stubbed.
- **#163/#168 PHP / C#**: C# csproj ownership and ProjectReference discovery work without Git. PHP reads the installed Composer ClassLoader PSR-4 mappings, including local path packages; before installation, declared local path repositories (including wildcard URLs) supply mappings from their package manifests. Symlinked vendor paths resolve to their project source. External/vendor-only destinations are explicitly declined. A throwing PHPUnit subject reached before the assertion counter increments is executed Red, not a skipped test; mixed passing/skipped provider rows are accepted.
- **#169 Julia**: comma-separated relative imports (`using .Existing, .Fresh`) select/wrap the matching included module. The binding probe loads non-relative imports in the project environment, so imported stdlib functions such as `LinearAlgebra.dot` and `issymmetric` are not shadowed with throwing stubs.
